title: Tracing a single call and a chain of calls

videos.script: A customer asks Marginalia's assistant when delivery is free. The answer comes back in under a second. It is wrong, and nothing on the screen says so. {{answer}} This lesson puts a record behind every answer. One span around a model call: what was asked for, what answered, how many tokens, how long. {{span}} Then the whole chain. The question is embedded, the documents are searched, the model writes, the citations are checked. Each step is a span, nested under one root. {{tree}} Read the tree and the time is easy to place. Nine tenths of it is the model. {{time}} Read the attributes and the wrong answer explains itself. One chunk survived the search, and it was about the wrong kind of delivery. {{why}} A library can write these spans for you. Look at what it keeps when it does. {{library}} And every trace has an id, which is what feedback, scores and support tickets will join to. {{id}} What a trace cannot tell you is whether the answer was right. That takes the second half of the course. {{end}}
